facts.fact: Environmental degradation takes four forms: deforestation, pollution, soil degradation/desertification and biodiversity loss.
Pollution is a negative externality: social cost exceeds private cost, so the good is overproduced.
The tragedy of the commons (Garrett Hardin, 1968) is overuse of an open-access shared resource.
The Environmental Kuznets Curve is an inverted U: degradation rises with income, then falls.
Clean air is a public good — non-excludable and non-rival — so markets under-supply it.
The tragedy of the commons was named by Garrett Hardin in 1968.
A Pigouvian tax equals the marginal external cost, internalising the externality.
Cap-and-trade fixes total emissions and lets firms trade permits so cuts happen where cheapest.
The Coase theorem: clear property rights and cheap bargaining can solve pollution privately.
Polluter Pays and Precautionary principles were read into Article 21 (Vellore Citizens, 1996).
Command-and-control sets emission limits; market-based tools price pollution.
The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is the umbrella law passed after the Bhopal tragedy (1984).
The National Green Tribunal was set up in 2010.
Wildlife 1972, Water 1974, Forest Conservation 1980, Air 1981.
EIA is governed by the EIA Notification 2006; Category A projects are cleared by the MoEFCC and include public consultation.
The CPCB was created by the Water Act, 1974.
India committed to net-zero emissions by 2070.
Panchamrit (COP26, 2021): 500 GW non-fossil, 50% renewables, 45% intensity cut, 1 billion-tonne cut by 2030.
India's 2022 updated NDC cuts emissions intensity of GDP by 45% from 2005 by 2030.
NAPCC (2008) has eight missions; ISA was co-founded by India and France; Mission LiFE promotes green lifestyles.
The 2022 NDC targets about 50% non-fossil power capacity by 2030.
CCTS 2023 was notified under the Energy Conservation Act 2001 (amended 2022) and is administered by BEE.
CCTS has a compliance mechanism and an offset mechanism.
ESCerts (PAT), RECs, Carbon Credit Certificates (CCTS) and Sovereign Green Bonds are distinct instruments.
India issued its first Sovereign Green Bonds in 2022-23 (₹16,000 crore).
Green budgeting uses the budget process to advance environmental objectives.
The Grid Controller of India runs the CCTS registry.
Green GDP adjusts GDP downward for depletion of natural resources and environmental degradation.
NDP deducts depreciation of man-made capital; Green GDP also deducts natural-capital loss.
SEEA: 1993 handbook, Central Framework standard 2012, Ecosystem Accounting 2021.
MoSPI has published EnviStats India annually since 2018; India was in the NCAVES project.
Partha Dasgupta led India's Green National Accounts group (2013); the Dasgupta Review (2021) was commissioned by the UK Treasury.
Uttarakhand pioneered the Gross Environment Product in India.
Adjusted Net Savings is a World Bank measure; the Inclusive Wealth Index is UNEP's.
Ecosystem services: provisioning, regulating, cultural, supporting.
The Ramsar Convention on wetlands dates from 1971.
The 1972 Stockholm Conference created UNEP; 5 June is World Environment Day.
CITES (1973) regulates trade in endangered species.
CMS (Bonn Convention, 1979) protects migratory species.
The Montreal Protocol (1987) protects the ozone layer; the Kigali Amendment (2016) phases down HFCs.
The Vienna Convention (1985) is the ozone framework treaty.
Basel Convention (1989) controls transboundary movement of hazardous waste.
Rotterdam (1998) covers prior informed consent for hazardous chemicals; Stockholm (2001) covers POPs.
The Minamata Convention (2013) deals with mercury.
The 1992 Rio Earth Summit produced the UNFCCC, CBD and Agenda 21.
UNCCD (desertification) followed in 1994.
The Kyoto Protocol (1997, in force 2005) set binding cuts for Annex I countries with CDM, JI and emissions trading.
The Paris Agreement (2015) entered into force on 4 November 2016 with five-yearly NDCs and Article 6 markets.
Cartagena Protocol (2000) covers biosafety; Nagoya Protocol (2010) covers access and benefit-sharing.
The Nagoya Protocol (2010) covers access to genetic resources and benefit-sharing.
The Kunming–Montreal GBF (2022) set the 30×30 target.
The Brundtland Report "Our Common Future" (1987) defined sustainable development.
PAGE was launched at Rio+20 (2012) (UPSC 2018).
CBDR-RC is the Rio principle of Common But Differentiated Responsibilities.
REDD+ means reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation (UNFCCC).
One carbon credit equals one tonne of CO₂-equivalent (UPSC 2011).
The Green Climate Fund was set up at Cancún (2010) and is based in Songdo, South Korea.
COP27 (Sharm el-Sheikh, 2022) agreed the Loss and Damage Fund.
COP28 (Dubai, 2023) completed the first Global Stocktake.
COP29 (Baku, 2024) set the NCQG of US$300 billion a year by 2035.
COP30 was held at Belém, Brazil (2025), launching the Tropical Forest Forever Facility.
COP31 is at Antalya, Türkiye, 9-20 November 2026; COP32 at Addis Ababa (2027).
Kolleru Lake in Andhra Pradesh is a Ramsar site (2002).
Article 48A (DPSP) on environment protection was added by the 42nd Amendment (1976).
Article 51A(g) makes protecting the natural environment a Fundamental Duty.
M.C. Mehta (Oleum gas leak, 1986) created absolute liability for hazardous industries.
The Public Liability Insurance Act dates from 1991.
The Biological Diversity Act (2002) set up the National Biodiversity Authority at Chennai.
The Forest Rights Act was passed in 2006.
NGT appeals go to the Supreme Court within 90 days; principal bench New Delhi.
The CAMPA Act (2016) governs compensatory afforestation funds.
The Wild Life (Protection) Amendment 2022 cut schedules to four and incorporated CITES.
The Forest (Conservation) Amendment 2023 renamed the Act Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam.
The Jan Vishwas Act 2023 replaced jail with penalties for minor offences under the EPA, Air and Water Acts.
The Solid Waste Management Rules and Plastic Waste Management Rules date from 2016.
Identified single-use plastic items were banned from 1 July 2022.
E-Waste and Battery Waste Management Rules came in 2022, with EPR.
Extended Producer Responsibility makes producers collect and recycle their products after use.
A circular economy cuts raw-material input and waste and thereby GHG emissions (UPSC 2025).
Pollution types (source mind map): air, water, soil, noise, light and radiation.
Eutrophication is nutrient overload of water bodies, mainly from farm run-off.
Air pollution causes acid rain and ozone depletion besides respiratory disease.
Noise is regulated by the Noise Pollution Rules, 2000.
NCAP (January 2019) covers 131 non-attainment cities with a 40% PM10 cut target by 2025-26.
The National Air Quality Index (2014) uses eight pollutants.
Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada are AP's NCAP non-attainment cities.
The LG Polymers styrene leak at Visakhapatnam (7 May 2020) drew NGT interim damages of ₹50 crore.
India's non-fossil installed capacity crossed 50% in 2025, five years early.
National Green Hydrogen Mission (January 2023): ₹19,744 crore and 5 million tonnes a year by 2030.
SIGHT is the incentive programme under the Green Hydrogen Mission.
Green hydrogen can decarbonise fertiliser plants, refineries and steel plants (UPSC 2023).
PM Surya Ghar (Feb 2024) gives rooftop solar with up to 300 free units a month to 1 crore homes.
PM-KUSUM (2019) promotes solar pumps; the National Solar Mission dates from 2010.
The International Solar Alliance was launched at COP21 (2015) and is headquartered in Gurugram.
Coal was nationalised in 1971-73 under Indira Gandhi; blocks now go by auction (UPSC 2019).
The Supreme Court cancelled 204 coal blocks in 2014; commercial coal mining opened in 2020.
India's coal output crossed 1 billion tonnes in 2024-25 but it still imports coking coal.
The ₹400-a-tonne Clean Environment Cess on coal became GST compensation cess (2017) and was removed by GST 2.0.
District Mineral Foundations (MMDR Amendment 2015) protect the interests of people affected by mining (UPSC 2016).
DMF contributions are 30% of royalty for pre-2015 leases and 10% for auctioned leases; spent under PMKKKY.
Carbon markets are among the most widespread climate tools and do not transfer resources to the State (UPSC 2023).
BRSR is mandated by SEBI (not the RBI) for the top 1,000 listed companies and is largely non-financial (UPSC 2025).
The Green Credit Programme was notified in October 2023 and launched globally at COP28.
GEAC must approve any import of GM food (UPSC 2024).
In a recession the likely step is more spending on public projects (UPSC 2020).
When the government provides a good free, the opportunity cost shifts to taxpayers (UPSC 2018).
NTPC Green's green hydrogen hub at Pudimadaka (Anakapalli) is ~₹1.85 lakh crore; foundation laid 8 January 2025.
AP targets 160 GW of green energy by 2047.
AP has about 14,833 MW of renewable capacity (August 2026) and added 3,866 MW in 2025-26.
Pinnapuram (Nandyal) hosts an integrated renewable-plus-pumped-storage project.
Harita AP targets 37% green cover by 2030 and 50% by 2047.
Budget 2026-27 gives ₹20,000 crore over five years for CCUS.
The Disaster Management Act was passed in 2005; NDMA is chaired by the Prime Minister.
The NDRF was set up in 2006 as the specialist response force.
The Sendai Framework covers 2015-2030.
CDRI is India-led (2019) and headquartered in New Delhi.
Polavaram dam raises displacement of tribal families in the Godavari valley.
Operation Kolleru (2006) removed illegal fish tanks from Kolleru Lake.
Resettlement follows the RFCTLARR Act, 2013.
Cyclone Hudhud (October 2014) struck Visakhapatnam.
Cyclone Titli (October 2018) hit Srikakulam district.
Cyclone Michaung (December 2023) made landfall near Bapatla.
Cyclone Montha (October 2025) made landfall near Narasapuram.
APSDMA runs disaster management in AP; Coringa mangroves buffer storms.
